facts.text: For years fans assumed director Pierre Chevalier was a pseudonym for Spanish cult filmmaker Jess Franco. Reviewers say that's not true; Franco had no hand in this film.
Star Howard Vernon first played Dr. Orloff in Jess Franco's 1962 chiller The Awful Dr. Orloff. This film is a loose, Franco-less spin on that character.
Howard Vernon appeared in about 40 of Jess Franco's films and nearly 200 productions overall, working with Godard, Fritz Lang, and Woody Allen too.
During WWII, Howard Vernon (Professor Orloff) was a presenter on the Nazi-controlled Paris TV station Fernsehsender Paris, since he was Swiss and bilingual.
Some scenes with nudity were shot twice: once bare, once with the actresses dressed or covered. That let distributors tailor the film to different markets.
The film went by many titles: Orloff and the Invisible Man, Orloff Against the Invisible Man, Dr. Orloff's Invisible Monster, and The Love Life of an Invisible Man.
Filmed in France at the Château de Verderonne, in the Oise region north of Paris. The nearby village cemetery also appears in the film.
Mondo Digital's review calls the film a mix of 'Gothic ambience and Ed Wood insanity.' It's a European exploitation oddity.
Co-star Paco Valladares (Dr. Garondet) was the Spanish dubbing voice of Clint Eastwood in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.
The film was a French-Spanish co-production, released by Eurociné in 1970. It reached Canada in 1974 as Secret Love Life of the Invisible Man.
Fernando Sancho, who plays the gamekeeper, was a Spaghetti Western staple. He also played a Turkish sergeant in Lawrence of Arabia.
Wizard Video put this out on American VHS as The Invisible Dead. The Orloff name only returned with the later DVD release.
Director Pierre Chevalier began as an assistant to Marcel Carné and René Clément. He later made erotic and porn films, plus this one horror cult item.
